key_insight: Increasing infrared excitation intensity drives a Mott-like crossover in 2D (BA)₂PbI₄ from exciton-dominated behavior toward a dense electron–hole plasma, alongside a switch from saturable to reverse saturable absorption.
engineering_relevance: The intensity-tunable optical response could support infrared all-optical switching, although the study does not demonstrate solar-cell performance gains.
method: Probe nonlinear absorption and refraction using femtosecond Z-scan measurements at 1030 nm.
Use excitation whose two-photon energy is resonant with the excitonic transition.
Track carrier dynamics with intensity-dependent transient absorption spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an intensity-dependent absorption switch and a long-lived carrier population above the estimated Mott density, supporting the proposed Mott-like transition.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical switching thresholds, operational stability data, or device-level validation.
paper_title: Intensity-driven Mott-like transition in a 2D Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite
